comment: Frame 016, printed p. 10: the second example of subtraction, 1144 less 144; halving, place by place, with the half of an odd unit written as thirty sixtieths and the half of an odd ten as five in the place before; doubling, from the highest place; the beginning of multiplication: the products of the numbers from one to nine to be known, and the placing of the two numbers in the table.

observations: The page number «( 10 )» stands at the head of the page, centred. The page has no footnotes and no signature.

L01-L03: the example of subtraction is one thousand one hundred and forty-four («mille centum quadraginta quatuor») less «.c.xliiii.», one hundred and forty-four, written «.c.» and «xliiii.» with one point between them; L03 ends «hoc modo.», in this way, without the figure and without the four points of a gap. L33: «.ccx.iiiior», two hundred and fourteen, «iiii» with «or» raised, after «.ccx.».
L07-L09: the half of an odd unit is written as «triginta partem ex sexaginta», thirty sixtieths, placed under the place as «.xxx.».
L32: the second «u» of «numerum» is broken, its two stems printed as short strokes; transcribed «numerum».

Spaces at punctuation (rule of tools/punct.py: after a mark, a space where the gap is at least 12 px or two thirds of the median word space of the line; before a mark, where it is at least 10 px): L09 «.xxx.: deinde», the colon close to the point (8 px), without a space; L24 «unum et .ix.», with a wider space (31 px) before the point; the colon of L32 «sinistram:» is close to the word (6 px).
copy_matter: A reader's notes in pencil: «or / XLIIII» in the left margin beside L01-L02, a reading of «.xliiii.» as quadraginta quatuor; L03, a dot after «modo.» (darkest pixel 107, where the printed point is 22) and faint erased writing to the right of it; «quod» in the left margin beside L10, with «et» marked by a stroke; L11, «paris,» underlined and a slash after it; L11, a stroke over «loco»; L13, a stroke over «fuerit»; «quod / quod» in the left margin beside L15-L16, with strokes under «Et» (L15, L16); L27, a small comma-shaped mark at the base line between «eis» and «secundum», not in the ink of the print. Not part of the edition.
